Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, says he committed N500m to the acquisition and dissemination of the authorised biography of late President Muhammadu Buhari, because the former president was an “iroko tree” upon whom he leaned during the most difficult moments of his life. According to a statement issued Saturday by the Muhammadu Buhari Foundation, Rabiu, made the remarks when he appeared at the public presentation of the book, Buhari: The Authorised Biography. Rabiu, who was represented by former Senator representing Zamfara North, Lawal Shuaibu, delivered a personal tribute to the late Buhari The business tycoon drew on private memories, saying his relationship with Buhari spanned friendship, family ties, mentorship and moments of acute business adversity. He said, “President Muhammadu Buhari was everything to me. He was a father, a mentor, a trusted friend and a pillar of strength to my family and me.” He said the relationship prompted his N500m commitment to preserving the memory of the former president who passed away in July 2025 at a London medical facility. The reassurance, Rabiu said, moved him to tears. “For that, I will remain eternally grateful to him. It is something I will never forget for as long as I live,” he stated. Jonathan’s sacrifice rare among politicians – LP chair Jonathan reveals reason for conceding defeat to Buhari Jonathan, Shettima, others pay tributes to Buhari He said “Buhari’s intervention had saved the business.” Rabiu also described Buhari as a “cherished family friend” whose role in his life exceeded the formal boundaries of politics, government and commerce. He recounted, “He was an iroko tree upon which I leaned when my strength was failing.” Rabiu described Buhari as a man of integrity, humility and simplicity, who also prized loyalty, friendship and family. “To the nation, he was a President and a statesman to me and my family, he was much more,” he stated. According to the statement, the presentation was devoted to placing Buhari’s life before the judgement of history through the three-volume authorised biography written by Dr. Udu Yakubu. Rabiu said the books deserved support because Buhari’s “life, service and legacy deserve to be remembered and celebrated for generations to come.” He said his N500m acquisition commitment is based on his personal memory of Buhari as father figure, mentor, friend and protector. It is also meant to preserve Buhari’s life and record through books intended to pass into homes, libraries, educational institutions and the wider national archive, said Rabiu.
